title: Pallava Rock-Cut Era Begins
description: Narasimhavarman I initiates the rock-cut monument tradition at Mahabalipuram, including Arjuna's Penance and the Pancha Rathas, laying the artistic groundwork that later produced the Shore Temple.

title: Shore Temple Constructed
description: Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) commissions the Shore Temple, built from dressed granite blocks rather than carved from a single rock — a shift toward structural temple architecture.

title: Pallava Decline
description: Following Rajasimha's reign, Pallava political power gradually wanes under pressure from the Chola dynasty, though the temple continues in active worship.

title: Chola Period
description: The Chola dynasty absorbs the region and continues South Indian temple-building traditions influenced by Pallava structural innovation, including the vimana form pioneered at the Shore Temple.

title: European Colonial-Era Accounts
description: European travelers and colonial administrators document Mahabalipuram, including early written references to a temple structure visible from the sea, contributing to the site's modern rediscovery.

title: Archaeological Documentation
description: The Archaeological Survey of India undertakes systematic study, conservation assessment, and protection measures for the Shore Temple and the wider Mahabalipuram monument group.

title: UNESCO World Heritage Listing
description: The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram, including the Shore Temple, is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognizing its outstanding universal cultural value.

title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
description: The 2004 tsunami temporarily exposes submerged structures off the coast near the temple, renewing scientific interest in the possibility of additional Pallava-era structures beneath the sea.

title: Ongoing Conservation & Digital Documentation
description: ASI conservation continues to address coastal erosion damage, while digital preservation initiatives — including projects like HeritageVerse — aim to create lasting, accessible records of the site.
